messages:
alex: Noticing a reproducible perf spike on A100 with CUDA 12.3 driver when runs go past ~8k-12k tokens. Kernel eviction/GPU memory churn in logs. Can we align on short-term mitigations and partner escalation?

maria_s: Which marketplace/runtime images picked up 12.3? We should stop any automatic rollouts.

alex: Looks like redwood/runtime:latest on some clusters pulled cuda:12.3 base. Short log snippet: ```
[2026-03-20 14:02:11] step 10000: token_latency_ms=48 -> step 10050: token_latency_ms=72
[WARN] kernel_reclaim: eviction triggered on SM 2
Stack: driver=535.54, cuda=12.3, cudnn=8.6
```

kevin_h: ROCm smoke passes for similar long-seq tests. This looks CUDA driver-specific. I can run nvprof traces and Nsight snapshots to show kernel-level timeline.

rachel_ops: Immediate ops: 1) Marketplace: pause auto-promotion of images with cuda-12.3 2) Pin GA images to cuda-12.2 3) Create opt-in canary tag for experimenters. Jess  can you coordinate the marketplace hold?

jess_market: Yep I can flip promotion flag and create a redwood/runtime:cuda-12.3-experimental tag. Ill also add a note on the marketplace changelog so customers see it's opt-in.

samir: Opening partner escalation with NVIDIA now. Drafting brief with repro steps, logs, perf graphs, and Nsight capture request. Will ask for a driver patch or mitigation flags (e.g., kernel reclaim controls).

alex: One more mitigation idea: runtime-level knob to disable kernel-reclaim or force smaller batch window after long sequences. Worth adding while vendor investigates.

kevin_h: I'll land a CI job that runs a 12k-token streaming job nightly against the canary tag and upload perf traces to the ticket. Alert if 95th percentile token latency exceeds baseline by 25%.

rachel_ops: Also make sure Dedicated/reserved pools are using the pinned images. We should add an infra guard to block accidental canary promotion into reserved capacity.

nvidia-bot: [auto] Received escalation PRJ-4598 from Redwood. Ticket: https://partners.nvidia.com/cases/PRJ-4598. Status: intake accepted. Assigned to eng-driver-team.

samir: Added detailed reproducer and requested a signed hotfix build and a manifest we can pin in marketplace when available. Also requested a list of exact driver commits that changed scheduler behavior. Marked P1.

maria_s: I'll open the marketplace PR to pin runtime images to redwood/base:cuda-12.2-pinned and include a rollback job for any GA rollouts. PR will reference this ticket.

alex: Draft customer-facing blurb: "We identified a performance regression affecting long-context workloads on certain NVIDIA A100 configurations with CUDA 12.3. We have temporarily pinned our runtime images to CUDA 12.2 for production customers. Experimental images are available for testing. No action required for most customers." Thoughts?

jess_market: Good. I'll schedule the announcement hold: no marketplace release until partner confirms fix and we validate in staging -> canary -> prod gating.

kevin_h: After vendor patch arrives, plan: run vendor-signed driver in staging cluster (full long-seq smoke), if green promote to canary nodes for a week, then GA. I'll prepare rollback criteria and a perf dashboard.

rachel_ops: Ops checklist: block autoscaler from spinning up nodes with cuda-12.3 images, confirm monitoring alerts for long-seq regressions, and coordinate with support for customer tickets.

samir: NVIDIA responded to initial intake: "investigating kernel reclaim interaction with persistent KV caches; may provide a driver patch or recommended flag to disable reclaim." They asked for our Nsight captures. Link to partner case above.

alex: Perfect. Action items recap: samir -> drive partner P1 + attach traces, jess_market -> pause marketplace promotions + pin PR, maria_s -> create pin PR + customer comm, kevin_h -> nightly long-seq smoke + traces and alert, rachel_ops -> infra guard + monitoring rules. Keep replies here and paste partner updates.

maria_s: PR opened: https://marketplace.redwood/pr/7234 -> pins to cuda-12.2-pinned and adds changelog note.

alex: Thanks all. Please flag if you see any related regressions on other GPU families; otherwise we continue with the gate plan. :handshake:
